content:
zara_manager: Quick question
were planning an interim promotion (acting Staff Eng) for someone covering an open role for ~3 months. Director approved. Do we change title in HRIS, bump base, or use an acting/title-only note? Want to avoid complications when they revert.

lina_hr: Good Q. Options: 1) temporary "acting" title in HRIS with no base change, 2) temporary base supplement (one-time monthly stipend) processed as Compensation Adjustment, or 3) permanent promotion if expected to last and meet banding. For a true interim we usually do acting title + stipend.

omar_comp: If you do a stipend, submit Comp Adjustment with duration and amount. Stipends are taxed as income and treated as one-time payments each pay period; they don't change base or band. If you want a base bump, that's a Role Change packet and is considered permanent.

michael_payroll: Practical payroll notes: acting title-only  no payroll change needed. Stipends need comp adj form by payroll cutoff for the month it's paid. If you later convert to permanent promo, payroll will need clear notes to avoid double-paying stipend vs base.

elaine_legal: Also document the reversion policy in writing (manager + director email) so employee understands terms. For EU-based employees, check local law about unilateral pay reductions on reversion
sometimes you need written consent.

zara_manager: For performance reviews
will acting title affect next cycle calibration or comp eligibility?

lina_hr: Acting title alone shouldn't change level calibration for performance cycles. If you make it permanent (Role Change) before calibration cutoff, it will affect banding and calibration. Communicate explicitly to People Ops if you want it considered.

omar_comp: If manager wants to consider them for a promo during interim, best to submit permanent Role Change with full evidence. Otherwise stipend + acting title is clean and low risk.

zara_manager: Thanks. One more: how do we record end date of acting assignment so it's auto-reverted?

lina_hr: In the HR portal put "acting assignment end date" in the packet comments and attach director email that calls out the date. People Ops will add a temp title note and set a reminder to follow up 2 weeks before end date.

michael_payroll: If stipend, include start/end pay periods and employee ID. Payroll will create the one-time payment schedule; if converted to base before end date, notify payroll to cancel remaining stipends.

elaine_legal: If there's any market or equity implications, flag Compensation early. Also include a short written agreement to avoid later disputes.

zara_manager: Great, we'll do acting title + monthly stipend for 3 months and attach director note with end date. I'll submit comp adj + portal comments tonight and ping when done.

people-ops-bot: Checklist: For acting assignments: include employee name, ID, acting title, start date, end date, stipend amount (if any), director approval, manager rationale. HR portal: https://hr.redwood.internal/role-change, Comp Adj: https://comp.redwood.internal/comp-adjust. Payroll deadlines: https://payroll.redwood.internal/deadlines.
